sections.heading: C — Sharing the road: pedestrians, emergency vehicles, trucks and buses, school buses and motorcycles
sections.markdown:
## C — Sharing the road: pedestrians, emergency vehicles, trucks and buses, school buses and motorcycles

FACT_ID: sec09-F01 | anchor: A37
Pedestrians have the right-of-way at street crossings, but they too must obey traffic control signals. [A37]
Source: [A37 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec09-F02 | anchor: A37
Where there is no traffic signal, you must stop for a pedestrian in a crosswalk whether it is marked or unmarked. [A37]
Source: [A37 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec09-F03 | anchor: A37
Watch especially for deaf, blind or mobility-impaired pedestrians, who may not see or hear traffic well and may need more time to cross. [A37]
Source: [A37 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec09-F04 | anchor: A37
A crosswalk is where pedestrians may cross and drivers must stop for them; some are painted, others are not, and most intersections have one even without markings. [A37]
Source: [A37 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec09-F05 | anchor: A37
You may not pass any vehicle that has stopped at a crosswalk. [A37]
Source: [A37 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec09-F06 | anchor: A37
You must yield to pedestrians when turning on green and when making a permitted turn on red after stopping. [A37]
Source: [A37 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec09-F07 | anchor: A37
Police cars, ambulances and fire engines have the right-of-way when their sirens and flashing lights are on. [A37]
Source: [A37 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec09-F08 | anchor: A37
As soon as you see or hear an emergency vehicle signaling, get as close to the road edge as you can, keep out of intersections and stay stopped until it passes. [A37]
Source: [A37 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec09-F09 | anchor: A37
You may not pass an emergency vehicle using its signals in your direction unless it stops or a police officer directs you to pass. [A37]
Source: [A37 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec09-F10 | anchor: A37
Approaching a stopped emergency vehicle, tow truck or other service vehicle, move to a lane not right next to it; if you cannot, slow to a safe speed and be ready to stop. [A37]
Source: [A37 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec09-F11 | anchor: A37
Trucks need more room than cars and swing wide at intersections, often moving left before a right turn. [A37]
Source: [A37 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec09-F12 | anchor: A37
Passing a truck on its right is risky, so wait to see whether a truck that drifts left is about to turn right before you pass. [A37]
Source: [A37 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec09-F13 | anchor: A38
Never squeeze along the right side of a truck starting a turn at an intersection, or you may be trapped between it and the curb. [A38]
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec09-F14 | anchor: A38
Pass a same-direction truck quickly, and return to its lane only once both of its headlights show in your rear-view mirror. [A38]
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec09-F15 | anchor: A38
Stopping beyond a stop line can put your vehicle in the path of trucks turning from the cross street. [A38]
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec09-F16 | anchor: A38
Never cut in front of a truck: a fully loaded one can top 80,000 pounds and need a football field's length to stop, while most cars weigh only 2,000 pounds. [A38]
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec09-F17 | anchor: A38
Trucks have 4 large blind spots, called no-zones, where other vehicles vanish from the driver's view. [A38]
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec09-F18 | anchor: A38
Side no-zones lie on both sides of trucks and buses; if you cannot see the driver's face in the side mirror, the driver cannot see you. [A38]
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec09-F19 | anchor: A38
A truck's right-side blind spot runs the full length of the trailer and reaches out 3 lanes. [A38]
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec09-F20 | anchor: A38
Trucks and buses have huge rear no-zones, so do not tailgate them; the driver cannot see you and you have no escape if they stop suddenly. [A38]
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec09-F21 | anchor: A38
Truck and bus drivers need nearly twice the time and room that cars need to stop, so do not pull in front of them too soon after passing. [A38]
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec09-F22 | anchor: A38
After passing a truck or bus, wait until both of its headlights appear in your rear-view mirror before moving in front, and then do not slow down. [A38]
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec09-F23 | anchor: A38
Never cross behind a backing truck; its driver has no rear-view mirror, and hundreds of people are killed or hurt each year this way. [A38]
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec09-F24 | anchor: A38
When a school bus stops with flashing red lights, stop at least 20 feet from its back if you are behind it, or 20 feet from its front if you are ahead of it. [A38]
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec09-F25 | anchor: A39
Stay stopped until the school bus moves again or switches off its flashing red lights. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec09-F26 | anchor: A39
On a multi-lane road split by a physical barrier, you do not stop for a school bus on the far side of the barrier. [A39]
Why it matters: the exception the manual names is a physical barrier dividing the road.
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec09-F27 | anchor: A39
Motorcyclists share the same rights and privileges as other drivers, yet are 6 times more likely than car drivers to be hurt in a crash. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec09-F28 | anchor: A39
Yield to an oncoming motorcycle when you turn left; failing to can bring a citation with significant penalties, and drivers are at fault in over half of car-motorcycle crashes. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec09-F29 | anchor: A39
Look twice, using mirrors and a shoulder check, before merging or changing lanes, because a small motorcycle can hide in a blind spot. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec09-F30 | anchor: A39
Never share a lane with a motorcycle; riders may use the whole lane and shift within it to avoid hazards, handle wind and be seen. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec09-F31 | anchor: A39
Keep a following distance of at least 3 to 4 seconds behind a motorcycle, since riders may slow without brake lights showing. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec09-F32 | anchor: A39
When passing a motorcycle leave plenty of room, and pull back in only once its headlight shows in your rear-view mirror; if a rider passes you, hold your speed. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec09-F33 | anchor: A39
Near a group of riders, signal early and wait for room, merge between riders only with enough safe space, and for a small group consider slowing to let it pass. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0039]

Glossary: crosswalk — a place where pedestrians cross and drivers must stop, marked or not [A37]. No-zone — a large blind spot around a truck or bus [A38]. Through lane — a lane that continues straight [A41].
Memory aid: if you cannot see the truck driver's face or mirrors, the driver cannot see you [A38].
Misconception: an unpainted intersection is not free of crosswalks; most intersections have one even when it is unmarked [A37].

items.why: the no-zones are spatial areas around a truck shown on a diagram, so learners need a top-down positional drill rather than text-only cards
